subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: The product
hotspots.description: The water molecule on the right is the product — the new substance the reaction creates from the hydrogen and oxygen reactants.
hotspots.positionHint: The water molecule on the right side of the equation.
hotspots.function: Shows the new substance created by the reaction.

hotspots.label: Forming the product
hotspots.description: When the form layer is on, the product assembles atom by atom from the reactant atoms — the reaction made visible.
hotspots.positionHint: The water molecule assembling in the center-right when the layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the product being assembled by the reaction.

hotspots.label: Inherited atoms
hotspots.description: Every atom in this product came from the reactants — same atoms, new connections. None are created or destroyed.
hotspots.positionHint: The atoms of the product, highlighted with trails back to the reactants.
hotspots.function: Shows that product atoms come from the reactants.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A miniature chemical equation floats centered — reactants on the left, an arrow, and a freshly formed water product on the right — lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Ball-stick molecules in CPK colors: hydrogen warm off-white, oxygen muted red. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (molecular-green / amber / coral accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Hydrogen spheres: warm off-white, roughness ~0.5. Oxygen spheres: muted red, roughness ~0.45. Bond rods: thin graphite cylinders. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a chemical equation for making water, focused on the product, built to be read as 'right side = the new substance the reaction creates.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a flat equation scene — LEFT: two hydrogen molecules (H₂) and one oxygen molecule (O₂) as in the reactant component; CENTER: a flat arrow tile (app-rendered glyph); RIGHT: one water molecule (H₂O) slightly brighter than the reactants, as if freshly formed.

2) PRODUCT FORMING (toggleable layer): the reaction runs — reactant bonds break and the product's water molecule assembles atom by atom on the right (app animates atoms gliding into place).

3) ATOM INHERITANCE (toggleable layer): the product's atoms each light up with a faint trail back to the reactant molecule they came from — making 'same atoms, rearranged' visible.

Camera: framed so all three zones fit with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: Reactant_H2_01-02, Reactant_O2, Product_H2O, EquationArrow, AtomInheritanceTrails. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
